_comment: Hand-authored design decisions that a profiler cannot infer.
The profiler reports what IS in the files. This overlay says what we WANT in Db2:
table names, column renames, keys, constraints and deliberate type overrides.
Type overrides matter more than they look. The profiler sizes integers from the
range it observed, so against small fixtures a key column comes out SMALLINT.
Real transactions_data.csv has ~13M rows. Pinning key types here makes the DDL
independent of how much data happened to be profiled.

watermark.ddl: TIMESTAMP NOT NULL GENERATED ALWAYS FOR EACH ROW ON UPDATE AS ROW CHANGE TIMESTAMP
_comment: Engine-maintained, not application-maintained. Verified on Db2 11.5.9.0:
set on INSERT, advanced on UPDATE, untouched rows left alone.
KNOWN GAP: does not capture DELETEs. That limitation is deliberate and is
documented in docs/roadmap.md under change-capture patterns.

tables.comment: Customer master. One row per client.
Card master. Many cards per customer.

card_number.name: CARD_NUMBER
card_number.comment: Synthetic. Never cast a PAN to a number.
card_number.override_reason: a PAN is an identifier; BIGINT would lose leading digits and imply arithmetic is meaningful

expires.name: EXPIRES_YM
expires.comment: MM/YYYY. No day component, so DATE would invent one.

cvv.name: CVV
cvv.comment: Zero-padded: 4 values in the real file begin with 0.
cvv.override_reason: SMALLINT would turn '023' into 23; a CVV is an identifier, not a quantity

has_chip.name: HAS_CHIP
has_chip.override_reason: keep the source YES/NO wording; normalising to 0/1 belongs in silver, not bronze

card_on_dark_web.name: CARD_ON_DARK_WEB
card_on_dark_web.override_reason: same as has_chip - bronze preserves source values as-is

tables.comment: Card transaction fact. The large table; ~13M rows in the real dataset.

indexes.name: IX_TXN_TS
indexes.comment: The watermark predicate hits this on every incremental run.

indexes.name: IX_TXN_WATERMARK
indexes.comment: Fabric filters on this. Without it, every run is a table scan.

date.name: TXN_TS
date.comment: Renamed: DATE is a Db2 reserved word.

amount.name: AMOUNT
amount.comment: DECIMAL, never FLOAT. Control totals must tie exactly.

merchant_state.name: MERCHANT_STATE
comment: Not a US state code. The column mixes 2-letter US states with full
country names; the longest observed is 'Saint Vincent and the
Grenadines' at 32 characters. 11.75% are null.
VARCHAR(16) truncated it. Sized to 64 for headroom.

zip.name: MERCHANT_ZIP
comment: Arrives float-formatted as '58523.0' — the source already treated a
postcode as a number, which is also why the leading zeros are gone
(lowest observed is 1001, i.e. Massachusetts 01001). The '.0' is
stripped in prepare; the lost leading zero cannot be recovered here
and is a genuine source-data defect worth showing the customer.
12.42% are null.
zip.override_reason: a ZIP is an identifier, not a quantity; leading zeros must survive

mcc.name: MCC_CODE
mcc.override_reason: joins to MCC_CODES.MCC_CODE; both sides must be the same type

tables.comment: Merchant category dimension, flattened from a JSON code->description map.
Fraud labels, flattened from {'target': {txn_id: 'Yes'|'No'}}. Partial coverage by design.

comment: IBM AML set. A single wide table whose only job is volume.
No natural key in the source, so a generated identity column supplies one.

synthetic_key.name: AML_TXN_ID
synthetic_key.ddl: BIGINT NOT NULL GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY (START WITH 1, INCREMENT BY 1)

Timestamp.name: TXN_TS
Timestamp.comment: A real timestamp - this is what makes the watermark clean.

Account_dup4.name: ACCOUNT_TO
comment: The source header contains the name 'Account' TWICE, literally.
This is the second one (position 4, zero-based), which the profiler
disambiguates as 'Account_dup4'. It is NOT called 'Account.1' —
that is the pandas convention, and assuming it cost a silent
failure: the overlay mapped a column that does not exist, so the
destination account would have been dropped from the load entirely.

Amount Received.name: AMOUNT_RECEIVED
comment: Scale 6, not 2. 148,151 rows in HI-Small carry more than two
decimal places (the crypto rows go down to 0.000001), so
DECIMAL(19,2) would round them to 0.00 on load — no error, no
rejected row, just quietly missing money and control totals that
no longer tie.
